@graph.headline: One Page Can't Do Five Jobs: The Website Architecture That Gets Metro Detroit Businesses Found
@graph.description: The median dedicated page converts at 4.02% against 2.35% for a general one, and search engines rank pages, not businesses. Here is the page architecture — one job per page — that gets a Metro Detroit business found and chosen, plus the thin-content trap that punishes padding.

about.name: Website architecture as a growth decision — one page per service and per service area, the thin-content trap, internal-link wiring, and why structured multi-page sites are what AI answer engines cite

keywords: how many pages should a website have

mainEntity.name: How many pages should a small business website have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most small business sites perform best with five to ten focused core pages to start, growing toward seven to fifteen; local service businesses do well in the eight-to-twenty range. The right number comes from counting your services and priority areas, not from a template.

mainEntity.name: Does every service need its own page?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you offer three or more distinct services, yes. A dedicated page per service is a top on-page factor for local rankings, and dedicated pages convert at roughly double the rate of general ones. A single well-built services page is fine if you offer only one or two services.

mainEntity.name: When do I need service-area or location pages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only for the towns that drive real revenue, and only when you can write something genuinely specific about each. Businesses with optimized location pages see about 37% more leads, but a page per town built by swapping the place name is thin content that can hurt the whole site.

mainEntity.name: Can too many pages hurt my SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the extra pages are thin. Search engines judge overall site quality, and a large share of unhelpful pages can pull down your good pages. More pages help only when each one is substantive and earns its place.

mainEntity.name: What pages does every local business website need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four to start: a home page, an about page, a contact page, and at least one service page (a services hub if you sell several). From that core you add one page per service and per priority service area.

mainEntity.name: How does site architecture affect AI search like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI engines cite structured, multi-page sites far more than single landing pages. ChatGPT cites only about 15% of the pages it retrieves, and FAQ schema plus first-paragraph answers raise citation odds by roughly 40%. A site with a page per question is far more citable than one page trying to cover everything.

mainEntity.name: Do I need internal links between my pages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Internal links pass authority to the pages that need it, improve crawl efficiency by 40 to 70%, and can lift rankings by up to 40%. Keep every important page within three clicks of the home page and eliminate orphan pages.
